SIDEWAYS audio attribution

Recorded tyre sample
Title: Car tire squeal / skid loop (tires_squal_loop.wav)
Original recording: audible-edge (Tom Haigh)
Loop edit: qubodup
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/car-tire-squeal-skid-loop
Original recording source: https://freesound.org/people/audible-edge/sounds/71739/
License of the loop adaptation: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported
License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
Legal text: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/legalcode

SIDEWAYS modifications: resampled from 96 kHz mono PCM24 to 48 kHz mono
PCM16; bandpass filtering at 280 Hz and 10 kHz to reduce recorded engine
bleed; DC removal; normalized output; 30 ms loop crossfade. Playback gain,
small pitch variation and stereo position follow the actual wheel contact,
slip speed, normal load and dissipated tyre work. Stored as PCM data in
samples.js so no network request is needed during play.

No endorsement by the original authors is implied.

Player engine and native mechanical sources
MotorLab SDK 1.6.3, supplied by the user. Player sound comes from the same
live engine session as crank physics. Source configurations and simulation
remain in sdk/. Continuous contact, wind, NOS and some mechanical layers are
original procedural game effects. NOS sound is an arcade treatment, not a
measured nitrous injection recording. Recorded interface and world samples
are listed below.

Distant traffic engine bed
Generated offline from MotorLab 1.5.0 I4, approximately 1800 RPM, then
resampled to 24 kHz PCM16 with DC removal, bandpass and 50 ms loop seam.
Used only for lightweight ambient NPC engine audio. NPC pitch and gain
follow traffic speed/load estimates; it is not a second player-engine clock.

V6 music and acoustic kit
========================

Band phrase
Title: Funked Up
Author: Joth
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/funked-up
Original file: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/Funked%20Up.mp3
License: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
License: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
Changes: selected a twelve-bar phrase (33.103448 seconds, 87 BPM) starting
at 0.080 seconds; applied short edge fades and level trim; re-encoded to
128 kbit/s stereo MP3. The game adds separately scheduled acoustic drum
samples, filters and gain changes according to menu, driving and pursuit.
Embedded in music-track.js; no streaming or runtime download.
The published source describes guitar, bass, Rhodes and drumset. No claim
is made about the original recording technique or live performance.

Changes: selected a 4.60-second wail starting at 0.80 seconds; made a
20 ms loop crossfade; filtered at 200 Hz and 8 kHz; removed DC, normalized
and resampled to 24 kHz mono PCM16. Embedded in kit.js. The source is a
designed emergency-siren sound, not represented as a field recording.

All V6 source and adapted-file hashes, sample rates and selected durations
are recorded in qa/audio-v6-assets.json. CC0 source authors are credited
voluntarily; no endorsement is implied. Each license applies to its own
listed material. The MotorLab SDK remains under its supplied license.

V7 pursuit music, dispatch and ambience
======================================

Pursuit arrangement
Title: Skateboard-car-chase
Author: bertsz
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/skateboard-car-chase
Original archive: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/ld44.zip
Original file: main1_not_looped.flac
License: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
Changes: selected sixteen bars at 118 BPM (32.542372881 seconds), starting
at 4.067796610 seconds; level trim, short edge fades and stereo MP3 encode
at 128 kbit/s. Two synchronized eight-bar sections crossfade with pursuit
pressure. Search filters the arrangement; escape releases it over several
seconds before the cruising phrase returns. Added VCSL percussion uses
its own gain, pan and timing. No original recording technique is asserted.
Embedded in chase-track.js, without runtime downloads.

Contextual radio speech
1. Police Priority Traffic Dispatch, by bluelinevibes
   https://freesound.org/people/bluelinevibes/sounds/752406/
   Public preview used:
   https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/752/752406_16289147-hq.mp3
2. Dispatcher2.wav, by ciaranm758 (Harsfield Police Chatter)
   https://freesound.org/people/ciaranm758/sounds/422839/
   Public preview used:
   https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/422/422839_6613451-hq.mp3
3. Reply2.wav, by ciaranm758 (Harsfield Police Chatter)
   https://freesound.org/people/ciaranm758/sounds/422842/
   Public preview used:
   https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/422/422842_6613451-hq.mp3
Each source license: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
Changes: band-limited at 290 Hz and 3.7 kHz, converted to mono 24 kHz,
normalized, DC removed, short edge fades, embedded PCM16 in radio-kit.js.
These are authored radio snippets. They are not represented as recordings
of a real police operation. Tactical on-screen summaries are game-generated
and are not claimed to be verbatim transcripts of the sampled speech.

Author: synth2

Stereo night ambience
Title: Southern Summer Evening Ambience with Crickets 2
Author: RyanKingArt
Source: https://freesound.org/people/RyanKingArt/sounds/746363/
Public preview used:
https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/746/746363_11069322-hq.mp3
License: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
The author describes a recording made in Middle Tennessee on July 13, 2024.
Changes: selected seven seconds starting at two seconds, filtered at
180 Hz and 7.2 kHz, converted to 16 kHz stereo, DC removed, normalized,
made a 200 ms equal-power seam and embedded PCM16 in ambient-kit.js.

Wind, water and industrial beds remain procedural broadband textures.
Facade reflection delays are derived from map geometry and camera basis;
they are signal processing, not field recordings. All V7 source and adapted
hashes are in qa/audio-v7-assets.json. CC0 credits do not imply endorsement.

V8 driving music
================

Title: Super Wreck Roadway
Author: Umplix
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/super-wreck-roadway
Original file: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/super_wreck_roadway_loop.wav
License: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
Changes: retained the complete 56-bar rock arrangement, trimmed the final
5 ms to 134.4 seconds, multiplied gain by 0.63 to retain headroom from the
floating-point WAV, applied 6 ms edge fades, and encoded stereo 44.1 kHz
MP3 at 128 kbit/s. Tempo is inferred as 100 BPM from onset autocorrelation.
No claim is made about the original recording or instrument technique.
This replaces the earlier Joth cruising phrase in the shipped V8 soundtrack.
The bertsz pursuit arrangement and recorded VCSL percussion remain, with
stronger pursuit gain and additional focus/reading filtering.
Source and adapted hashes are in qa/audio-v8-assets.json.

V11 radio, native NPC voices and spatial acoustics
=================================================

Five additional spoken radio recordings and a radio click are embedded in
radio-kit.js. These are recorded authored radio lines, not live police traffic.
The game chooses different replies per event, avoids immediate repetitions,
expires stale tactical messages and retains captions as game summaries.
Captions are not presented as verbatim transcripts of these recordings.

Author: ciaranm758, Harsfield Police Chatter
- Reply1.wav: https://freesound.org/people/ciaranm758/sounds/422843/
  https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/422/422843_6613451-hq.mp3
- Reply3.wav: https://freesound.org/people/ciaranm758/sounds/422847/
  https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/422/422847_6613451-hq.mp3
- RadioIn.wav: https://freesound.org/people/ciaranm758/sounds/422844/
  https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/422/422844_6613451-hq.mp3
Author: alean, Radio Voice line of military jargon
- Affirmative 2.wav: https://freesound.org/people/alean/sounds/520308/
  https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/520/520308_3234030-hq.mp3
- Ruger that.wav: https://freesound.org/people/alean/sounds/520363/
  https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/520/520363_3234030-hq.mp3
- Standing by 2.wav: https://freesound.org/people/alean/sounds/520362/
  https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/520/520362_3234030-hq.mp3
Each source license: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal.
https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
Changes: public previews decoded, mono24kHz,260Hz high-pass and3650Hz
low-pass, DC removal, silence-only edge trimming, fixed peak normalization
and10ms edge fades. No generated speech or voice pitch shifting.
Exact source/adapted hashes and trims: qa/audio-v11-assets.json.

The shipped NPC engines now use four new offline-rendered MotorLab1.6.3
beds: inline four, turbo inline six, V8 and twin rotor. Each is generated
from one native engine under a physical load near1800RPM, mixed to mono
24kHz, DC removed, level trimmed and given a60ms loop seam. Nearby cars
use the matching family with simulated RPM/load, distance, Doppler and
camera-relative stereo. These replace the earlier I4-only traffic bed in
world playback; they are lightweight NPC audio, not separate native player
clocks. Generation code and sample hashes are in qa/build-npc-audio-v11.mjs
and qa/npc-audio-v11-assets.json. The user-supplied SDK terms still apply.

Player and world reflections retain stereo direction. Facade distance also
reduces high-frequency echo energy. Dock09 now uses its container/building
colliders to measure reflection paths; small posts and low kerbs do not
create false acoustic walls. No environment or radio asset is fetched at
runtime. No author endorsement is implied.
